function: Joint optimization of BS precoding vectors and RIS phase shifts to maximize sum rate in a multi-RIS multiuser downlink with practical amplitude-phase coupling, using DDPG (p. 1-3).
system: BS with 16 antennas, 4 passive reflecting RISs of 16 elements, 1-4 single-antenna UEs per RIS, practical phase-shift model, mmWave (carrier not stated) (p. 2, 4).
method: DDPG deep reinforcement learning, actor with two 1024-unit hidden layers, trained with random or fixed numbers of UEs; state is UE presence, previous action, rates (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulator: mmWave Saleh-Valenzuela channel, path loss from 3GPP Release 16 (TR 38.901), angles from ref. [20]; testing over 1,000 environments (p. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Trained with random (1-4 per RIS) or fixed (2 or 4 per RIS) numbers of UEs; tested on random 4-16 UEs and other maximum transmit powers (p. 4-5).
baselines: BCD and WMMSE-PI (optimization-based, single RIS, ideal reflection) and DDQN (learned, earlier DRL for RIS) (p. 1, 4-5).
metrics: Average reward and achievable sum rate (bps/Hz) versus maximum transmit power, convergence over episodes, and FLOPs (p. 4-5).
complexity: 3.71 x 10^6 FLOPs on average in online inference for DDPG (p. 4) versus 7.03 x 10^8 FLOPs for BCD (p. 5).
openness: none; no code or data link, the channel comes from the authors' own simulator (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "The channel coefficient of the direct path followed the mmWave Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) channel model"; p. 4: "referring to 3GPP standard release 16 [19]" only for the path loss, so a custom simulator.
q2_support: p. 5: "The trained weights used from these three scenarios were applicable to the scenario of the random UE number"; weights trained with a fixed 2 or 4 UEs per RIS are tested with random 4-16 UEs.
q3_support: p. 5: "DDPG outperformed DDQN by 63%" and "the achievable rate of BCD outperformed DDPG by 89.9%"; DDQN [3] is an earlier learned method, BCD [17] is non-learned, both compared on achievable rate.
q4_support: p. 4: "floating-point operations (FLOPs) on average"; DDPG inference needs 3.71 x 10^6 FLOPs, and BCD 7.03 x 10^8 FLOPs (p. 5).
q5_support: p. 4: "The following setup was considered in the simulations"; the channel is generated by the authors' own simulator, and no code link, data link, or public dataset is given.
notes: Included letter, area 3 (RIS): DDPG designs the BS precoder and the RIS phase shifts under a practical amplitude-phase model. q1 is 0 because the Saleh-Valenzuela simulator takes only its path loss from 3GPP TR 38.901 and its angles from ref. [20]. q2 rests on Fig. 5, where the fixed-UE models are tested with a random number of UEs. The non-learned baselines apply only to a single RIS with ideal reflection (p. 4).
